name: questdb
summary: High-performance local time-series database with HTTP, PostgreSQL-wire, and Influx line-protocol interfaces.
why_it_matters: QuestDB remains a plausible future option for high-volume metrics and event analytics, but no current production scenario declares or uses it. Keeping the capability as a blueprint avoids maintaining an unused Docker and shell implementation.
when_to_use: A scenario has a demonstrated need for high-throughput time-series ingestion beyond its existing storage backend.
A metrics or observability product needs time-series SQL queries or Influx line-protocol compatibility.
The owning scenario commits to operating, testing, and declaring QuestDB as an active dependency.

platform_support.notes: The prior implementation used Docker. A future implementation should reassess Docker against a managed local-service design and state the desktop-bundling trade-off explicitly.

prerequisites: A concrete owning scenario with a declared resource dependency
A validated retention, ingestion, and query workload
An explicit runtime choice and platform-support plan
implementation_notes: Start from the resource maturity and migration playbook before restoring an implementation.
Prefer the lightest feasible runtime archetype; do not assume Docker is the default for desktop use cases.
Implement configuration, lifecycle, diagnostics, and tests through the Go-native resource surface without Bash dependencies.
Replace the historical Node-RED and shell integration sketches with a tested consumer-owned integration.
operational_notes: Define data retention and storage growth limits before enabling ingestion.
Health checks must verify query/ingestion readiness, not only that a container is running.
Document the chosen HTTP, PostgreSQL-wire, or Influx line-protocol contract for each consumer.
risks: No active production consumer currently proves the maintenance cost.
A Docker-first implementation adds a host daemon requirement that may not fit desktop bundles.
Metrics storage can accumulate unbounded data without explicit retention policy.
